subject: chemistry
question_text: Calculate the weight of 0.1 mole of sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃).

verification.note: Chapter 5 (Stoichiometry) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.66-72), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Formula and molar mass
steps.why: This is the mole relation used in reverse: moles multiplied by molar mass gives grams. The molar mass of Na₂CO₃ must be computed from atomic weights on the page.
common_mistakes: Using 23 once instead of twice for the two sodium atoms.
steps.memory_tip: Moles to grams: multiply by the molar mass. Grams to moles: divide.
steps.margin_note: The computed GMW 106 g mol⁻¹ earns this mark.

steps.label: The answer with its unit
steps.why: One tenth of a mole weighs one tenth of the molar mass: 0.1 × 106 = 10.6 g.
common_mistakes: Misplacing the decimal and writing 1.06 g or 106 g.
steps.memory_tip: A tenth of a mole is a tenth of 106: shift the decimal one place.

insider_note: The mark sits in the molar-mass sum 46 + 12 + 48 = 106 written on the page, not in the one-line multiplication that follows it.
